recent_articles.title: Frequent disruptions in legislatures pose a serious challenge to democratic institutions: Om Birla - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Om Birla**, Speaker of the Lok Sabha, emphasized that frequent disruptions in legislative institutions pose a challenge to democratic principles. He urged **state and central legislatures** to promote conduct aligned with public expectations and meaningful discussion. The second conference of the **Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) India Region Zone-II (North Zone)** concluded with four resolutions aimed at making legislative institutions more effective, accountable, and people-centric.  These resolutions are expected to contribute to the progress of parliamentary and democratic institutions in India.

recent_articles.title: Sikkim Suicide Rate Falls 15.8% In 2 Years As Focus On Mental Health Expands
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sikkim** has experienced a 15.8% decline in its suicide rate over two years, according to the **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)** data. The rate dropped from 43.1 per lakh population in 2022 to 36.3 in 2024.  **Sikkim Health Minister GT Dhungel** attributed this improvement to collaborative efforts by various departments, mental health professionals, schools, NGOs, local bodies, police personnel and community groups. He emphasized the importance of sustained mental health interventions and community support for further reducing suicides and improving access to care in the state.

recent_articles.title: Missing Sikkim Family Found Dead After Vehicle Plunges Into Teesta River
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Four residents of Sikkim**, including a five-year-old child, were found dead inside a submerged vehicle recovered from the Teesta River on Sunday after a two-day search operation. The victims, identified as Smarika Neopaney (28), Shaibya Neopaney (27), Tika Dahal (27), and Ditya Chettri (5), went missing while traveling from Gangtok to Siliguri on Friday.  The family's last known communication was reported to have originated from the Rambi area, prompting a search operation involving personnel from the **National Disaster Response Force**, **West Bengal Police**, and local officials. The vehicle is believed to have plunged into the river after an accident along the highway.

recent_articles.title: NSE investor accounts cross 26 crore milestone as mobile trading and tier-2/3 cities drive participation - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Stock Exchange of India (NSE)** reported over 4.3 crore new investor accounts in the past year, representing nearly 17% of its total account base. This growth is attributed to sustained retail interest despite geopolitical uncertainty and market volatility, fueled by initiatives like Investor Awareness Programs and a simplified KYC framework. The exchange's Investor Protection Fund stands at Rs 2,890 crore as of April 30, 2026. Maharashtra leads with the highest number of accounts, followed by Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, West Bengal, and Rajasthan.

recent_articles.title: 1965-Built Monastery Thangu Sertok Gumpa Destroyed In Sikkim Fire, Religious Artefacts Damaged
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A fire destroyed the **Thangu Sertok Gumpa** monastery and two nearby houses in North Sikkim on June 5th. The blaze, reportedly caused by an electrical short circuit, spread rapidly through the structure, leaving no chance to salvage any religious or cultural artifacts.  The monastery, built in 1965, held immense religious and cultural significance for the local community. Despite efforts to contain the flames, the fire reduced the monastery to ashes. No casualties were reported but significant property damage occurred.

recent_articles.title: Goa’s early date with monsoon, Maharashtra sees onset too | Bangalore News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** reported that the southwest monsoon further advanced into parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Goa, Andhra Pradesh, Mizoram and Manipur on Saturday. The monsoon may have arrived over northeast India but its progress into the entire region is delayed.  Heavy rainfall has been reported in Kerala, Meghalaya, Andaman and Nicobar islands, Odisha and Bihar since Friday due to an upper-air circulation off Kerala coast. The IMD predicts heavy rainfall for the next five days in Kerala, Karnataka, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal.

recent_articles.title: Twinkle Khanna’s ‘travel lighter’ message highlights burden of emotional baggage | Destination-of-the-week News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twinkle Khanna**, an actor-turned-author, recently encouraged travelers to "travel lighter" by downsizing their emotional baggage. **Khanna** drew a parallel between physical luggage and emotional burdens, suggesting that letting go of unnecessary baggage can lead to a more enjoyable travel experience. Travel experts like **DK Ghatani**, CEO of Sikkim Expeditions, agree, emphasizing the benefits of packing light in terms of mobility, flexibility, and reduced stress.  Psychologist **Neha Cadabam** emphasizes that addressing unresolved emotional experiences through practices like journaling and therapy is crucial for managing baggage and fostering emotional resilience.

recent_articles.title: Twinkle Khanna’s ‘travel lighter’ message highlights burden of emotional baggage | Destination-of-the-week News - The Indian Express
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Twinkle Khanna**, an actor-turned-author, recently encouraged travelers to "travel lighter" by minimizing both physical and emotional baggage. **DK Ghatani**, a travel consultant and CEO of Sikkim Expeditions, agrees that packing light enhances the travel experience by reducing stress and improving mobility. **Neha Cadabam**, a senior psychologist and executive director at Cadabam’s Hospitals, highlights that emotional baggage can negatively impact both travel and daily life, but emphasizes that processing these emotions through journaling, mindfulness, therapy, or honest conversations is crucial for developing emotional resilience.

recent_articles.title: Ladakh: Towards People’s Rule
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Centre** and representatives of the **Apex Body of Ladakh (ABL)** and **Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA)** have reached an "in-principle" agreement on restoring democracy in Ladakh, providing constitutional safeguards under provisions similar to Article 371 A, F, and G.  These provisions are applicable in states like Nagaland, Sikkim, and Mizoram. The agreement includes granting legislative, executive, and financial powers to elected representatives through a UT-level Assembly, with the elected head having direct administrative control over the entire UT bureaucracy.  The agreement also safeguards land, environment, culture, and jobs under Article 371.  While both parties expressed optimism about this step forward, they emphasized that further discussions are needed before finalizing the proposal.

recent_articles.title: “If I can do it, anybody can” Shape of Momo Director Tribeny Rai’s message to aspiring filmmakers - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A 14-year-old Indian-American, **Shrey Parikh**, won the 2026 Scripps National Spelling Bee but faced online racist comments. A dust storm in Rajasthan's Churu district caused widespread disruption, plunging parts of the region into darkness and halting daily life.  **Ram Charan, Janhvi Kapoor, Boman Irani, and Divyendu** spoke to India Today about their roles in the upcoming film "Peddi."

recent_articles.title: I never saw my representation on screen: Tribeny Rai on why she made 'Shape of Momo' - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: An alleged attack on **TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee** during his visit to Sonarpur, West Bengal sparked a major political showdown. Protesters hurled stones and eggs at his convoy, raising "chor chor" slogans, while the incident has drawn criticism from various political parties.

recent_articles.title: SIR enumeration phase begins in Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim and Manipur, says EC | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** of India has commenced the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim, and Manipur. The enumeration process involves Booth Level Officers (BLOs) visiting homes to collect and verify voter registration forms. Voters can submit their completed forms through BLOs or online.  Eligible voters must submit their forms by June 28th for inclusion in the draft electoral rolls. The **Election Commission** emphasizes that the SIR exercise aims to ensure accurate and comprehensive voter lists, including all eligible citizens aged 18 and above while removing ineligible individuals.

recent_articles.title: Phase 3 of SIR exercise begins in Odisha, Manipur, Sikkim, Mizoram - India Today
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission** initiated phase 3 of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in **Odisha**, **Mizoram**, **Sikkim**, and **Manipur**.  Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will conduct house-to-house visits to distribute, collect, and verify enumeration forms. Electors can submit their forms online or through BLOs. The deadline for submitting forms is June 28th, after which eligible voters can apply for registration as a new voter. **The four states** involved account for over 3.67 crore electors.

recent_articles.title: Sikkim govt withdraws odd-even restriction on movement of private vehicles except Gangtok: Here's what the order said | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sikkim's** government lifted the odd-even vehicle movement restrictions across all districts, except Gangtok, effective immediately. The decision was made after a review of fuel stocks revealed sufficient reserves of Motor Spirit (petrol) and High-Speed Diesel (diesel).  Private vehicles are now permitted to operate without the restrictions in all districts except the state capital.

recent_articles.title: Who drinks the most? Arunachal tops national chart, Himachal leads North - The Tribune
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)-6** revealed that **Arunachal Pradesh** has the highest proportion of men aged 15 and above reporting alcohol consumption, at 50.5 percent.  In northern India, **Himachal Pradesh** leads in alcohol consumption among men with 30.2 percent reporting consumption. The survey also found that **Chandigarh** has the highest overweight or obese population among men, with 48.5 percent of men falling into this category.

recent_articles.title: Rare 'intensive' revision in Bihar four months before polls - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** has ordered a special summary revision of electoral rolls in Bihar, marking a departure from its usual practice.  This revision differs from previous intensive revisions by utilizing the 2002-03 electoral roll as a base and incorporating a new pre-printed enumeration form for house-to-house verification. The ECI's decision to conduct this revision ahead of the assembly elections in October 2025 is unusual, as it has rarely ordered full state-wide intensive revisions so far out from the scheduled polls.  This move follows a pattern of the ECI conducting 'intensive' revision in specific areas of states based on various factors like population changes or electoral irregularities.

recent_articles.title: ECI set to roll out phase III of SIR in ‘coming days’ to cover 22 States, UTs - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is set to begin phase three of its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) voter list process in the coming days, covering nearly 40 crore electors across 17 states and five UTs.  This follows completion of SIR in 10 states and three UTs previously, which has successfully removed over 60 lakh deceased voters from the rolls. The ECI had initially delayed the rollout due to Assembly elections in several states but is now proceeding with the revision process.  The exercise aims to ensure accurate voter lists for upcoming elections.

recent_articles.title: Which party governs which State/UT: In maps - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** and its allies secured victories in Assam, Puducherry, and West Bengal, while the Congress-led UDF won in Tamil Nadu. **Suvendu Adhikari**, a BJP leader, is set to become the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal. The results mark a shift in the political landscape with the BJP or the NDA now governing 20 states and 2 Union Territories.

recent_articles.title: Census enumerators ID can be verified through QR code - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Lalit Jain**, Director of Census Operations (DCO), **Haryana**, has introduced QR code-enabled identity cards for enumerators to address concerns about authenticity.  Jain explained that residents can verify the legitimacy of enumerators by scanning the codes on their ID cards. The first phase of the digital census, which began on April 1, aims to cover over 30 lakh households across India. Residents are legally obligated to answer Census-related questions, and while there have been no cases of FIRs for non-response, local authorities will be involved in encouraging participation.  The second phase of the census, focusing on caste enumeration, is scheduled for February 2027.

recent_articles.title: Bangladesh seeks China support for Teesta restoration project - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bangladesh**’s new government has sought **China's** involvement in the Teesta River restoration project, a move that could strain relations with **India**.  The **Bangladesh** government is seeking to increase its share of the river's water under the 2011 Teesta water-sharing treaty, which has been blocked by **West Bengal**’s outgoing Chief Minister, **Mamata Banerjee**.  **China's** Foreign Minister, **Wang Yi**, pledged support for **Bangladesh's** new government and its development goals.

recent_articles.title: Gurugram gated societies not letting in enumerators; FIRs recommended against enumerators obstructing Census work - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Haryana** administration has recommended an FIR against two government school staff for alleged negligence in Census-related work and obstruction of duties.  **Gurugram Municipal Corporation Joint Commissioner Punit Kumar** stated that enumerators have been denied entry into several highrise apartment buildings, prompting him to write to RWAs to ensure their access. **Registrar General of India Mritunjay Kumar Narayan** flagged off awareness vans across Delhi for the ongoing Census 2027 public outreach campaign.  The first phase of the Census began on April 1 and will conclude by September 30, involving around 30 lakh enumerators.

recent_articles.title: Nepal lodges protest against India over long-running border dispute | Border Disputes News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Nepal**'s Ministry of Foreign Affairs lodged a protest against **India** after the country announced the resumption of a religious pilgrimage through the Lipulekh Pass, which is claimed by **Nepal** based on a 1816 treaty.  **India** maintains that the pass has been used for pilgrimages since 1954 and disputes **Nepal's** territorial claims. The dispute reignited after **India** agreed with **China** to resume the pilgrimage, which was suspended in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

recent_articles.title: India rejects Nepal’s objection to Kailash Manasarovar Yatra via Lipulekh Pass - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India** responded to **Nepal's** objection to the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra passing through Lipulekh Pass, stating that such territorial claims are "untenable." The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified that Lipulekh Pass has been a long-standing route for the pilgrimage since 1954 and that India remains open to dialogue with **Nepal** on all bilateral issues.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Around 82 lakh households have opted for self enumeration as field visits begin in 5 states - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Union government** announced that over 82 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the initial Houselisting and Housing Operations (HLO) phase of Census 2027. The exercise, which commenced on May 1st in several states including Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Rajasthan, aims to collect data about household facilities and demographics.  The HLO will continue until May 30th, with trained enumerators visiting each house for verification.

recent_articles.title: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra 2026: dates, routes, application process and all you need to know - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** announced the schedule for this year's Kailash Manasarovar Yatra, which will take place between June and August.  A computer-generated, random selection process will be used to select 20 batches of 50 tourists each, with one batch traveling through Uttarakhand via Lipulekh Pass and another through Sikkim via Nathu La Pass.

recent_articles.title: Earth Day 2026: How Nature walks, parks, and trails are sparking a new conservation movement - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rohit Girotra**, co-founder of the Bangalore Butterfly Club (BBC), has seen a surge in interest in butterflies and butterfly-focused activities. The BBC, which began in 2012, now boasts nearly 600 members and offers guided walks at Doresanipalya Forest Research Station.  **Ashok Sengupta**, another BBC co-founder, believes that butterfly watching is an easy portal into the natural world for children. **Isaac Kehimkar**, a naturalist and photographer, has documented over 40 Facebook groups dedicated to butterflies worldwide. These groups have helped raise awareness of these insects through social media and mobile cameras. Butterfly parks and trails are also becoming increasingly popular across India, with locations like Sammilan Shetty's Butterfly Park in Karnataka offering educational programs on butterfly conservation.

recent_articles.title: Govt claims women winning unreserved panchayat seats in ‘significant numbers’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Government** celebrated National Panchayati Raj Day, highlighting the progress of women's reservation in Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs).  While the Constitution mandates a 33% quota for women in urban and rural local bodies, 19 states have extended this provision to reserve 50% seats for women. However, data shows that the actual number of women representatives exceeds the prescribed quota in only 10 states/union territories, while four others fail to meet it.  The Ministry emphasized the increasing representation of women in PRIs, but acknowledged discrepancies between mandated and achieved quotas across various states.

recent_articles.title: Door-to-door visit by Census enumerators in eight States/U.T.s from April 16 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** announced the commencement of door-to-door enumeration for the first phase of the 2027 Population Census, known as the House Listing and Housing Operations (HLO). Beginning on April 16th in eight states and union territories including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, Odisha, Sikkim, and Delhi's NDMC area and Cantonment Board, enumerators will collect data for the HLO phase. This follows a 15-day self-enumeration period.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 9 States and 3 UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by **West Bengal**, with a net deletion of 83.86 lakh. The SIR phase II identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters across these states and UTs.  The consolidated electoral rolls saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Census of springs: 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Jal Shakti Ministry** released the first Spring Census Report, which revealed that 63.4% of springs in Kerala are under private ownership, significantly higher than other states like Karnataka and Tamil Nadu where public ownership dominates.  The report, covering Kerala, Karnataka, Ladakh, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, and Bihar, found that while Kerala has a high percentage of privately owned springs, the majority of springs across all surveyed states are publicly owned. The census, conducted by the **Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation**, aimed to inventory and map these critical water sources in response to depletion concerns.

recent_articles.title: Consolidated voters’ list of 12 States and UTs that underwent SIR Phase II trimmed by 10.2% - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Election Commission of India** announced the results of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, which saw a significant reduction in voter numbers across nine states and three Union Territories. **Uttar Pradesh** recorded the highest net deletion of voters at 2.04 crore, followed by West Bengal with 83.86 lakh.  The revision identified 67 lakh deceased voters and 1.28 crore duplicate voters for removal. The consolidated electoral rolls across these regions saw a reduction of 10.2%, bringing the number of active voters down to 45.81 crore.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027: Self-enumeration facility availed by 5.72 lakh households so far in first phase - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Registrar General of India (RGI)** announced that over 5.72 lakh households have utilized the self-enumeration facility during the first phase of the Census 2027. This digital initiative reflects growing participation in the census, with a special portal available for citizens in specific areas including Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Goa, Karnataka, Sikkim, Odisha, Lakshadweep, Mizoram, and Delhi's NDMC and Cantonment Board. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their details online, facilitating a faster and more convenient contribution to nation-building.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The **Election Commission** has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

recent_articles.title: The executive office without a limit - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Narendra Modi**, who has served as Prime Minister of India for over thirteen years, surpassed the record for longest tenure held by any elected official in the country.  The milestone raises questions about whether India's Constitution, which lacks term limits for the executive branch, is sufficient to ensure accountability and prevent abuse of power. The author argues that while elections are a key mechanism for holding leaders accountable, they are not enough to counter the advantages of prolonged incumbency. The author suggests restoring mechanisms like exempting votes on confidence motions from disqualification under the anti-defection law or introducing term limits for Prime Ministers and Chief Ministers.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: 55,000 households use Census self-enumeration portal on day one - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **President Droupadi Murmu**, **Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan**, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, and **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** were among the first to use the online self-enumeration portal for the 2027 Population Census in eight States and Union Territories. The portal, which launched on April 1, 2026, allows households to provide information about their housing conditions and assets before enumerators visit.  The first phase of the census, focusing on house listing operations and housing census (HLO), will run until May 15th in these areas. Data collected through self-enumeration is confidential and will be used for evidence-based planning and policy formulation.

recent_articles.title: Cabinet colleagues laud PM Modi’s record breaking 8,931 days in public office - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** surpassed former Sikkim Chief Minister Pawan Chamling's record of 8930 days in office, becoming India’s longest-serving head of government.  His Cabinet colleagues congratulated him, praising his dedication to the nation and commitment to service. **Modi**, the first Indian PM born after independence, has led his party to three consecutive Lok Sabha election victories.

recent_articles.title: Avalanche alert issued for high-altitude areas of Sikkim - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority** issued an avalanche alert for high-altitude regions of Gangtok and Pakyong districts due to changing weather conditions that increase the risk of snow instability. The alert, effective for the next 24 hours, advises people to stay updated with official alerts as avalanches are likely above 3,500 meters. Heavy rainfall has been affecting most parts of the Himalayan state since Friday morning, leading to road closures to Tsomgo Lake and Nathula from Gangtok due to heavy snowfall.

recent_articles.title: Tripura Government accommodating fake private universities, Opposition alleges - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **CPI(M)** and **Congress** members in the Tripura Assembly staged a walkout after bills were passed to establish three private universities.  **Sudip Roy Barman**, **Congress** leader, accused the government of engaging in suspicious financial corruption by allowing "bogus" institutions to operate. **Jitendra Chowdhury**, leader of the Opposition, alleged that the addresses and contact numbers provided by the applicants were not genuine, with one university's phone number belonging to a plywood factory. The bills are set to be introduced for another private university called "Dhanvantari University".
